chunks: Yaqub ibn Yazid from Sulayman ibn al-Husayn, the scribe of Ali ibn Yaqtin, said:
I counted for Ali ibn Yaqtin the number of people who paid him in one year: five hundred and fifty men. The least any of them gave him was seven hundred, and the most was ten thousand.
ai.seo_question: What was the range of financial contributions made by followers to Ali ibn Yaqtin in one year?
ai.summary: This hadith, found in the chapter on expiation for unintentional violations by pilgrims, illustrates the substantial financial capacity of the Shia community during the era of Ali ibn Yaqtin, the chief tax collector (al-Kharraj) for the Imams. The wide variance in contributions—from 700 to 10,000 dinars—among 550 individuals reflects the diverse economic statuses of the faithful and underscores the institutionalized nature of khums and sadaqat collection in early Shia society.
